stem: Two high schools in the same city want to know whether a new reading program improves reading scores. School X used the new program with all of its ninth graders for one year, and School Y did not. At the end of the year, School X's ninth graders had a higher average reading score than School Y's ninth graders. Which of the following is the main reason this result does not show that the program caused the higher scores?

choices.A: The study should have used more than two teachers at each school.
choices.B: Reading scores from two different schools can never be compared.
choices.C: The students at the two schools may differ in other ways, such as earlier reading skill, so the program's effect cannot be separated from the effect of the school.
choices.D: If the students had been randomly assigned to the program, no conclusion about the program would be possible.

solution: The program was given to a whole school, so every student who got it also attended School X.

Any other difference between the schools (students' earlier skills, teachers, resources) is mixed up with the program: the school is a confounding variable. Randomly assigning students to the program would remove this problem.

explanation.A: Incorrect. The number of teachers is not the issue; the program is confounded with the school.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Scores can be compared; the comparison just cannot show cause and effect here.
explanation.C: Correct. Because the program and the school go together, other differences between the schools could explain the result.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Random assignment is exactly what would allow a cause-and-effect conclusion.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'A': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'A', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
design = {'random_assignment': False, 'treatment_tied_to_school': True}
assert design['treatment_tied_to_school'] and not design['random_assignment']
ok = [k for k, v in choices.items() if 'differ in other ways' in v]
assert ok == [answer]
